problem: Today HAL made a music video that passed every automated check. Its owner watched it and said: not good enough.
loop_note: The owner sets the direction. HAL writes the lyrics, briefs the song and directs the video; artists the owner names become traits, never names in prompts.
create_note: Every call carries one session tag, so Livepeer Agent's cost report is the day's receipt: two songs and two music videos, 84 calls, $36.03.
review_lines: Lyrics: every take transcribed from its separated vocal; the chosen take sang 31 of 36 lines, 89% of words aligned.
Lip-sync: the audio in every returned clip is cross-correlated with the vocal segment sent. Offset 0 ms on all 16.
Edit: every cut on a bar line of the song's own beat grid; the choruses cut between two camera angles.
Master: EQ, width, glue compression, a soft clipper and an oversampled limiter to -10 LUFS.
When a provider job stalls, HAL cancels it (the reservation is refunded) and resubmits.
taste: Today's first cut passed every check. The owner said it still needed mastering, more production value, and to be much better in all aspects.
taste_fix: So HAL mastered it, added lip-sync from two angles, then wrote a new song about exactly that: being told it is not good enough, and making it again.
result_line: Lyrics by HAL, sung by MiniMax Music 3, picture by FLUX, Kling, PixVerse and OmniHuman, all through Livepeer Agent. Cut on the beat by HAL Studio.
close: Apache-2.0. Studio code, tests, and the receipt for every Livepeer Agent call are in the folder above.
